answers.core: It requires modifying the core resource and resource loader classes.
answers.workaround:
There are workarounds:

1. Whenever a call to load a resource is made, follow it with a manual check to see if the derived values have been computed.
2. Have custom property setters emit the changed signal and connect a method to it to compute derived values.
3. Have custom property setters directly compute the derived values, or call a method that does so.

While these do work, they involve a lot of additional boilerplate and conditional clutter, and introduce more opportunities for potential user-error. It's already extremely common for developers to use `NOTIFICATION_READY` (or more specifically, `_ready`) to handle any one-time setup code that needs to execute after all of the properties and children of a Node have been set. While not completely identical in behavior, `NOTIFICATION_POSTLOAD` provides a similar way of handling one-time setup calls that occur after all properties are set for Resources.

title: Add a Post-Load Notification to Resources
